instruction.name: bge
instruction.description: Branch if signed rj >= rd (measured not taken).

throughput.name: 8 not-taken branches
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --init 'addi.d $r4, $r0, 1; addi.d $r5, $r0, 2' --asm 'bge $r4, $r5, 0; bge $r4, $r5, 0; bge $r4, $r5, 0; bge $r4, $r5, 0; bge $r4, $r5, 0; bge $r4, $r5, 0; bge $r4, $r5, 0; bge $r4, $r5, 0'
throughput.notes: Not-taken branches run at 0.5 CPI. The marginal cost measured against a loop-only baseline improves with the number of static branches because one branch rides the loop branch slot (0.437 at 8 static branches for integer compares, converging to 0.5; 0.874 converging to 1.0 for FCC compares), so the saturated rate is recorded. Both ends are recorded as separate experiments, so the range is the spread between them.

throughput.name: 8 taken branches
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 8 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --init 'addi.d $r4, $r0, 2; addi.d $r5, $r0, 1' --asm 'bge $r4, $r5, 4; bge $r4, $r5, 4; bge $r4, $r5, 4; bge $r4, $r5, 4; bge $r4, $r5, 4; bge $r4, $r5, 4; bge $r4, $r5, 4; bge $r4, $r5, 4'
throughput.notes: Taken-branch throughput has two regimes. With a small static footprint (8 static branches, reused in a 1000-iteration loop) the branch retires at 1 CPI: measured 1.001, 1.000 and 1.002 for 2, 4 and 8 static branches. Once the static stream exceeds the BTB, each branch costs 3 cycles: 2.857 at 256 static branches and 3.006-3.007 from 1024 static branches on. The two ends are recorded as the range.

notes: No destination data dependency; latency is not defined. Taken-branch throughput spans 1 CPI (BTB-friendly) to 3 CPI (static stream beyond BTB capacity); not-taken branches run at 0.5 CPI.
